Re: Joint Representation — Sale of Membership Interests in Halstead Brothers Aggregates, LLC; Waiver of Conflict

Dear Rowan and Marguerite:

You have each asked this firm to represent you in connection with the proposed sale of the membership interests in Halstead Brothers Aggregates, LLC to Corvid Materials Partners, LP. Before we may do so, Georgia Rule of Professional Conduct 1.7 requires that we explain the risks of a joint representation and obtain your informed consent, confirmed in writing.

1. The common interest. You share the objective of selling the Company on the best terms available. On most questions — the purchase price, the scope of the representations and warranties, the escrow, the restrictive covenants — your interests are aligned, and a single firm can advance them more efficiently and at lower cost than two.

2. Where your interests may diverge. Your interests are not identical. You hold different percentages of the membership interests. The allocation of the purchase price among you, the allocation of the indemnity obligation and the escrow, the treatment of the seller notes, the scope and duration of the non-competition covenants each of you will sign, and the tax consequences of the transaction to each of you may affect you differently. A term that benefits one of you may cost the other.

3. No confidentiality between you. In a joint representation there is no attorney-client privilege between you as to communications with us on the matter. We will share with each of you any information material to the representation that we learn from the other. If either of you tells us something you do not want the other to know, we may have to withdraw.

4. What happens if a conflict becomes actual. If a disagreement arises between you that we cannot resolve, we may be required to withdraw from representing both of you, and you would each need to retain new counsel. That would cost you time and money. Information you have shared with us would not be privileged as between you in a later dispute.

5. Your right to separate counsel. You are each entitled to be represented by your own lawyer, and you are encouraged to consult independent counsel about this letter before signing it. You may revoke your consent at any time, though a revocation may require us to withdraw from representing both of you.

6. Scope. This consent covers the sale transaction described above and any related negotiation, documentation, and closing. It does not cover litigation between you, and we could not represent either of you against the other.

If you have read this letter, have had the opportunity to ask questions and to consult independent counsel, and consent to our joint representation on these terms, please sign below and return one copy to us.

Very truly yours,

VANDERMEER & ACHEBE LLP

/s/ Ifeoma Achebe
